chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Dizzy Gillespie fired from Calloway's band over a paper airplane
summary: Some musicians feared bop, others took it as a challenge. Horace tells that Dizzy threw a paper airplane that hit Cab, was fired, and then began playing bop with Parker.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Well, a few of them were frightened. But a lot of them thought it was a great challenge, and they were going to do it, and they did just that. I know a lot of musicians that did nothing but play hard swing, you know, before this, and I know a lot of them that transferred over to that type of playing and just do it, and, of course, they idolized Dizzy. You know, Dizzy -- I'll tell you a little, if I may, funny -- we're talking about Dizzy, inject this, you know. He was in Cab Calloway's band.
And he said Cab did him a favor. You know Cab fired him.

Do you know how he got fired from the band? Cab was out singing one sick at the time. This is authentic. And Dizzy will tell you this too. He was another guy that had the devil in him, you know, Dizzy.
Oh, listen, he's a funny cat.

Yeah, he made a little paper airplane, and he threw it, you know, and they go and they supposed to come back to you? Well, he did something wrong. This one didn't come back. It hit Cab in the back of the head.
And Cab knew this was Dizzy, so he gave him his notice.

This is how he got fired, on account of a little paper airplane that he hit him in the back of the head, while he was singing one of those things. Cab was always kind of, you know, tough, you know. But he said he did him a favor because as soon as he got out of there, he bought him one of these funny looking horns, you know, that turn all up in the air and stuff, started playing, started gigging around, and started playing this bebop, and he and Charlie Parker got together on it, one of those things. You know the story from now on.

So this is when he began to make his money, but he was in that band sitting in just as a side man at the Cotton Club playing parts (inaudible). So this little piece of paper hitting Cab on the back of the head, started playing -- it brought him didn't come back. So it started the fame and fortune.
